economy.summary: In June 2023 voted against House Bill 1500, a bill to increase Pennsylvania's minimum wage; the bill passed the House 103-100.
economy.short: Voted against 2023 bill to increase state minimum wage.

taxes.summary: His website says he supports meaningful tax, regulatory and welfare reforms, commonsense budgeting, and measures to protect children, the elderly and disabled.
taxes.short: Supports tax, regulatory and welfare reforms and commonsense budgeting.

abortion.summary: In July 2022 voted for Senate Bill 106, a proposed constitutional amendment package including language that the state constitution provides no right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion; the measure passed the House 107-92.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: In June 2025 voted against House Bill 1500, a cyber charter school bill addressing funding, transparency and accountability; the bill passed the House 104-98.
education.short: Voted against 2025 cyber charter funding and accountability bill.

energy.summary: In June 2023 voted against House Bill 1032, which created the Solar for Schools grant program to fund solar energy projects at schools; the bill passed the House 134-69 and became law in 2024.
energy.short: Voted against creating Solar for Schools grant program.

guns.summary: In May 2023 voted against House Bill 714, which would have expanded background check requirements for firearm sales by repealing exemptions for private long-gun transfers; the bill passed the House 109-92.
guns.short: Voted against expanding firearm sale background check requirements.

economy.summary: Said during the primary campaign that escalating prices, including gas prices, are hard for people regardless of political party.
economy.short: Says escalating prices are hard for people regardless of party.

taxes.summary: Says she will prioritize common-sense taxation if elected, alongside strong public schools, community-centered action, local economic growth and the dignity of all people; her public statements do not detail specific tax proposals.
taxes.short: Prioritizes common-sense taxation; no detailed tax proposals stated.

education.summary: At an April 2026 candidate forum, cited Pennsylvania's 45th-place national ranking in education funding and advocated new revenue strategies to strengthen public schools.
education.short: Advocates new revenue strategies to strengthen public school funding.
